A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SegAnyPET/PETS-5k study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite restructuring.

before.justification: v3 reports original segmentation experiments, training-strategy ablations, external validation, and CT/PET and tumor comparisons in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original segmentation measurements and ablations, including internal organ evaluation, AutoPET-Organ validation, and supplementary tumor and CT/PET comparisons.

M1.justification: The 3D architecture, interactive prediction procedure, CPCL losses, label rectification, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v4 expands the decoder-attention description without establishing an actual architectural or procedural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use PETS-5k, the 100-case AutoPET-Organ subset, and AutoPET tumor data, covering the same five training organs, seven additional organs, tumors, and CT/PET comparisons. Relocating external-validation results adds no coverage.

E2.justification: The same comparison methods remain, including SAM, MedSAM, SAM-Med3D variants, four task-specific architectures, and TotalSegmentator. Table 1 removes a training-data condition for retained methods; comparator identities otherwise match within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: v3 evaluates task-specific models trained on HQ data alone and on combined HQ/LQ data; v4 retains only the HQ condition. Dataset splits, prompting procedures, DSC metric, and SegAnyPET training settings remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish rerunning the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Removing the HQ/LQ comparison eliminates evidence testing whether additional noisy training data helps ordinary supervised models. The CPCL component ablation, external-distribution evaluation, prompting-time comparison, and tumor and CT/PET analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or result error bars. Predictive uncertainty used within CPCL is unchanged and does not constitute new statistical reporting of experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Table 1 loses four HQ+LQ result rows, including SwinUNETR's average DSC of 86.69. All retained numerical entries match, including external-organ results (v3 Table 5 to v4 Table 3), ablations, tumor results, and CT/PET comparisons. Retained qualitative figures also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the mathematical formulation of training remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 merely expands the verbal explanation of the existing DSC formula; no definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The same central contributions remain: PETS-5k, a universal 3D PET segmentation model, and CPCL. Claims of few-point segmentation of seen and unseen targets, superiority to existing models, and PET-specific novelty persist despite rewritten wording.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix C.2 explicitly qualifies generalization under simultaneous dataset and target shift, discusses inferiority to SAM-Med3D, and offers a five-versus-245-training-category explanation. v4 replaces this with a favorable external-generalization summary despite unchanged results. It also removes the discussion of noisy data degrading task-specific models and revises future directions. This substantially reduces applicability qualifications, although manual-prompting and scattered-tumor limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly describes decoder prompt self-attention and bidirectional cross-attention. Removing v3 Figure 5 also removes annotator experience ranges: 2–3 years for the junior annotator and 5–10 years for senior experts. Core implementation settings and the project access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same 45 works, but v4 drops the nnInteractive/SuperVoxel future-work connection and adds a joint-training role for existing structural-image datasets in Section 5. These are limited positioning changes rather than an expanded literature base.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, the dedicated Dataset Construction subsection is removed with information retained elsewhere, external-organ discussion enters the main experiments, and Appendix C is reorganized. Author-role notes are added and acknowledgements removed. v4 also introduces unresolved citation placeholders.

P2.justification: The external-organ table moves into the main text, several other tables are relocated, Figure 4 shrinks from two-column to one-column width, and the annotation-workflow figure is removed. Retained figures reuse the same visual content; captions and some table formatting change.

improvement.justification: Moving external results into the main text and clarifying decoder attention help readers. However, v4 removes the mixed-quality training comparison and the explicit combined-shift caveat: external left-upper-lung DSC still remains 19.14 versus SAM-Med3D's 64.18 at five points, without the earlier qualification. Broken citations and reduced Figure 4 legibility add reporting defects. These losses outweigh the limited gains, while the preserved method and most results limit the deterioration.
